help [<command>].out:
record   put <root> <slug> [<draft>...] [--json]
          check each draft (.draft/<old name>.md, or every draft) and write it into its
          section of the record files; a draft with errors stays, and exit 1. A draft that
          was put stays in .draft/.put/ until record stage-done: edit it and put it again
          Example: wf.mjs record put . demo 04-plan-api.md
record   get <root> <slug> <name>... [--section <heading>|--field <path>|--outline|--fields a,b]
             [--full] [--json]
          records as Markdown with frontmatter; several names in one call. --section prints
          the text under one ## heading, --field one value by a path of record set,
          --outline the fields and the ## headings with their sizes, --fields only those
          fields. A record over 20 KB prints its outline; --full prints all of it
          Example: wf.mjs record get . demo 04-plan-api --section "Steps"
record   draft <root> <slug> <name> [--json]
          write one record as its draft (.draft/<old name>.md) to change its body: edit the
          draft, then run record put
          Example: wf.mjs record draft . demo 04-plan-api
record   edit <root> <slug> <name> --section <heading> --from <file> | --replace <old> --with <new>
          change a body in place with the checks of put, and no draft: the text under one
          ## heading becomes the text of the file, or one exact text is replaced (refused
          when it matches nothing or more than once)
          Example: wf.mjs record edit . demo 05-implement-api --replace "- [ ] AC-2" --with "- [x] AC-2"
record   set <root> <slug> <name> <path=value>...
          merge fields into one record; a value reads as YAML, null deletes the field.
          Paths: field=v, a.b=v, list[<slug>].field=v, list[0].field=v, list+=v, list-=v.
          A value outside the enum of the schema is refused with the allowed values.
          A <name> of get, draft, edit and set is the record name with or without .md
          and its number, index, or a stage name (implement-api, 05-implement, review);
          a name that fits several records lists them, and exit 1
          Example: wf.mjs record set . demo 03-slice slices[api].status=in-progress
record   stage-done <root> <slug> <stage> [<slice>] [--next "<invocation>"] [--status s]
          the end of a stage in the index: current-stage, progress.<stage>, next-command,
          next-invocation (the default route of the stage, or --next) and workflow-files
          Example: wf.mjs record stage-done . demo implement api
record   list|where|migrate <root> <slug> [<old path>]
          the records of a workflow; the new place of an old path; move a workflow of
          the old layout into the record files, with redirects.yaml, and work out its
          derived fields again (total-slices, best-first-slice, the counts, the roster
          copies): run it on a workflow whose stored counts were written by hand
          Example: wf.mjs record list . demo
record   evidence <root> <slug> [--check] [--json]
          the size of the evidence; delete the oldest runs over the 200 MB cap (put does
          this too), never the newest run (--check: say what it would delete)
          Example: wf.mjs record evidence . demo --check

brief <root> <slug> <stage> [<slice>].out:
# Brief: implement codemode s3

The decision commands are `node "<plugin>/skills/wf/scripts/wf.mjs" decide <verb> "<root>" codemode ...`.

wf-dir: <root>/.ai/workflows/codemode

skill-dir: <plugin>/skills/wf
Each `<skill-dir>` in a file you read is this folder, and each `wf.mjs` command runs as `node "<plugin>/skills/wf/scripts/wf.mjs" …`. Never search the disk for wf.mjs, a script or the plugin folder.

Output boundary: write each commit message, PR text, doc and code comment in product language, with no workflow vocabulary (stage, command or skill names) and no `.ai/` paths, and leak-check it before you publish (<plugin>/skills/wf/reference/_output-boundary.md).
Standing steer: each entry under ## Rules, steers and notes binds this stage: a project rule, a live `steer` of the person, or a `note` that an earlier stage left for this slice. Honor it, never above a mandatory gate. A steer or rule that asks for a test, guard set or measured run after each step is honored once in the checks after the last step, on the final code: a step runs only format, lint and type checks (_workflow-rules.md, "A step only writes"), and give the relevant entries to each sub-agent you start (<plugin>/skills/wf/reference/_decisions.md).

## Card

- Build only the selected slice, in the order of its plan steps. Do not broaden the scope. Do not verify, review or ship.
- A step writes its tests with its code and does not run them. The first run of a new test is the slice run, after the last step.
- Before you write code against a dependency API that you have not read in this repo, and when a compile or type error names a library symbol (an unresolved reference, a missing export or attribute, a wrong signature), read the installed source with the `study-sources` skill, per [_source-study.md](<plugin>/skills/wf/reference/_source-study.md). Do not fix a library error by trial and error.
- Commit the code. Write the commit message in product language, per [_output-boundary.md](<plugin>/skills/wf/reference/_output-boundary.md).
- Resolve a small drift from the plan inside the scope, and record it in the implement artifact.
- When the brief has `## Changed since the plan` (a design the person approved again, or a project rule added after the plan), bring the steps of the plan to it with `record edit` before the first step, then build. A change that needs a new slice or drops an acceptance criterion is a question for the person.
- A plan or a slice reserves a decision for the person only as [_decision-classes.md](<plugin>/skills/wf/reference/_decision-classes.md) "A reservation needs the person's words" says.
- Settle an implementation-detail decision yourself, and record it. Do not settle an intent-bearing decision (per [_decision-classes.md](<plugin>/skills/wf/reference/_decision-classes.md)): run `decide answered` for its key, and when no live entry answers it, ask it. In a session, ask with the question tool ([_gate-question.md](<plugin>/skills/wf/reference/_gate-question.md)).
